task: Add Google Sign-In alongside the existing email/password auth, and rebuild the login and register screens in the visual language of the onboarding screens. 13 phases in four waves. User decisions fixed up front: @react-native-google-signin (native sheet) not expo-auth-session; auto-link to an existing password account only when email_verified is true; remake both auth screens; no Google Cloud client IDs exist yet, so client IDs come from env and the README documents the setup.
acceptanceCriteria: typecheck, lint and the full test suite pass at the repo root
the server verifies the Google ID token itself and never accepts an email or user id from the client
the email_verified gate runs before any lookup by email, so an unverified token cannot probe which emails have accounts
the join key is Google's sub, never email
POST /auth/google returns the same AuthTokenPair as /auth/login, so refresh rotation and family revocation are one code path, not two
a Google-only account pays the same argon2 cost on password login as an unknown email, so response timing does not reveal which accounts are Google-only
a Google-only account can still delete itself, and a token from a different Google account cannot delete it
the new route inherits the controller's 10 req/min/IP throttle rather than overriding it
no test file lives under apps/mobile/app, which Expo Router would turn into a route
every code file stays under 200 lines, including specs
EXPO_PUBLIC_* values actually reach the Metro bundle
app-verify fails loudly when Google is configured but the reversed client ID is missing from Info.plist
blastRadius: Authentication for the whole product, on both sides. The migration makes users.password_hash nullable, which reaches every existing reader of that column — two were found, one of which (deleteMe) would otherwise have made Google-only accounts permanently undeletable. PrimaryButton's gradient conversion touches five already-accepted screens. Two pre-existing defects were found and fixed along the way: EXPO_PUBLIC_* never reached the Metro bundle at all, because @expo/env resolves .env against the Expo project root and does not walk up to the repo root, so apiClient.baseURL was undefined in every build made the documented way; and EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL lacked the /api suffix the server's global prefix requires. Baseline before the work: api 96 tests, mobile 146, zero files over 200 lines.
contracts: POST /auth/google takes { id_token } only and returns the existing AuthTokenPair unchanged, so mobile reuses persistSession and there is exactly one token-persistence path. AuthService.issueTokenPairWithUser became public so GoogleAuthService issues sessions through the same rotation and family-revocation code rather than a parallel one. DELETE /users/me accepts exactly one of password or google_id_token. New error codes GOOGLE_TOKEN_INVALID and GOOGLE_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED are thrown explicitly by the business layer; the exception filter still never infers a domain code from an HTTP status. No provider column: the CHECK constraint (password_hash IS NOT NULL OR google_sub IS NOT NULL) is the invariant instead. Accepted risk: nonce is not validated because the native library does not mint one for this flow, so a leaked ID token is replayable within its lifetime, narrowed by TLS-only transport and a no-logging rule.
